tagline: The Home Depot is the world's largest home improvement retailer based on net sales for fiscal 2025.
hero_kpi_rationale: The Home Depot dominates the home improvement market, where same-store sales (SSS) are the primary indicator of organic growth and business health, directly reflecting customer traffic and residential demand dynamics.

kpis.name: Same-Store Sales
kpis.explanation: Growth in sales from stores open for more than one year, excluding the impact of openings or closures.
kpis.description: Same-store sales increased by 0.3% in 2025, compared to -1.8% in 2024, marking a rebound after a period of slowdown in the housing market.
kpis.signal: Positive organic growth after two negative years.

kpis.name: Net Sales
kpis.explanation: Total revenue from goods and services after deductions.
kpis.description: Revenue reached $164.7 billion in 2025, up 3.2%, driven by SRS and GMS (+$6.3 billion) despite an extra day in 2024.
kpis.signal: Growth driven by acquisitions and same-store sales.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Operating income divided by net sales.
kpis.description: Operating margin declined to 12.7% in 2025 from 13.5% in 2024, due to rising costs and post-acquisition investments.
kpis.signal: Slight margin contraction despite sales growth.

kpis.name: Inventory Turn
kpis.explanation: Number of times inventory is replenished during the year.
kpis.description: Inventory turnover decreased from 4.7 to 4.4, reflecting higher inventory levels in anticipation of demand or related to acquisition integrations.

kpis.name: Operating Cash Flow
kpis.explanation: Cash generated by the company's core business operations.
kpis.description: Operating cash flow amounted to $16.3 billion, used for dividends, debt repayment, and capex.
kpis.signal: Strong operating cash flow despite investments.

kpis.name: Number of Stores
kpis.explanation: Total number of stores open worldwide.
kpis.description: 10 new stores in the United States and 2 in Mexico bring the total to 2,359 stores in 2025.

kpis.name: Return on Invested Capital
kpis.explanation: Measure of the profitability of equity and debt capital employed in the business.
kpis.description: ROIC dropped to 25.7% in 2025 from 31.3% in 2024, due to increased debt and a pause in share buybacks.
kpis.signal: ROIC decline following the GMS acquisition.

kpis.name: Online Sales %
kpis.explanation: Proportion of sales generated through websites and mobile applications.
kpis.description: Online sales represented 15.9% of revenue in 2025, up 0.7 percentage points, with comparable online growth of +10.4%.

kpis.name: Acquisition Revenue Contribution
kpis.explanation: Portion of revenue generated by recently acquired businesses.
kpis.description: The SRS and GMS acquisitions contributed $6.3 billion to revenue in 2025.
kpis.signal: Major impact of SRS and GMS acquisitions on growth.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Montant total versé en dividendes par action sur l'année fiscale.

kpis.name: Capital Returned to Shareholders
kpis.explanation: Total annuel : dividendes versés + rachats d'actions (treasury).
kpis.description: Cumulative dividends + share buybacks (2021-2025) in billions USD.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Part du bénéfice net redistribuée. >80 % = potentiellement non soutenable.

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.description: Net income extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Net income of $14.156 Bn for last fiscal year (FY2025).

risks.title: Intense Competition from Retailers and Online Marketplaces
risks.score_rationale: Risk flagged early in Item 1A as 'highly competitive, highly fragmented'. Moderate but repeated language. Stable trend but structural in nature. High weight: direct competition from retailers and emergence of reseller marketplaces threaten dominant market position.

risks.title: Global Supply Chain Dependency
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly cited in forward-looking statements (tariffs, trade policy, supply chain diversification). Urgent language ('efforts and ability to continue to diversify'). Upward trend: tariffs and trade tensions mentioned as future risks. High weight for import-reliant retailer.

risks.title: Integration Risks from SRS and GMS Acquisitions
risks.score_rationale: Major acquisitions (SRS in fiscal 2024, GMS in fiscal 2025) adding 1,250+ locations. Forward-looking statements explicitly mention 'ability to recognize the anticipated benefits'. Cautious language on integration. New/upward trend: recent acquisitions. High weight: strategic portfolio transformation.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and Customer Data Protection
risks.score_rationale: Dedicated Item 1C on cybersecurity (page 22). Forward-looking statements explicitly cite 'cybersecurity events' as disruption risk. Language of increasing importance. Upward trend: cybersecurity becoming regulatory and operational priority. High weight for omnichannel retailer with massive data footprint.

risks.title: Labor Availability and Cost Pressures
risks.score_rationale: Forward-looking statements mention 'cost and availability of labor' and 'labor disputes' as risks. Moderate but explicit concern language. Upward trend: post-COVID labor market tensions. High weight: 2,359 stores plus 1,250 SRS locations require substantial workforce.

risks.title: Demand Volatility and Economic Cycles
risks.score_rationale: Forward-looking statements cite 'macroeconomic conditions', 'state of the housing and home improvement markets', 'state of the credit markets'. Repeated and nuanced language. Stable but cyclical trend. High weight: DIY/DIFM demand sensitive to mortgage rates and consumer confidence.

risks.title: Regulatory and Environmental Compliance
risks.score_rationale: Forward-looking statements mention 'legal and regulatory changes', 'executive orders', 'changes to tax laws'. Moderate language. Stable but growing trend (ESG, EPA). Moderate-to-high weight: multi-jurisdictional retailer (US, Canada, Mexico) with EH&S obligations.

risks.title: Supply Chain Disruptions and External Events
risks.score_rationale: Forward-looking statements cite 'events that could disrupt our business, supply chain, technology infrastructure' (tariffs, natural disasters, climate change, public health, labor disputes). Moderate concern language. Upward trend: accumulation of risks (geopolitical, climate). High weight for complex logistics network.

ai_positioning.summary: HD does not mention artificial intelligence in its report. There are no references to AI, machine learning, or related products.
